primary_finding: The mis-factoring is edge-addition where both source calculi identify worlds. A blocked minting step records acc.addEdge src wBlock, creating an obligation m.r (f src) (f wBlock) against branchSatisfiableIn's existentially-arbitrary model, whereas Massacci2000 Def 10.2 identifies worlds under a non-injective interpretation and ChagrovZakharyaschev1997 Thm 5.51 discharges the same condition by constructing S as a subset of the ambient relation. That asymmetry, not file size or bridge count, is the real seam.

memory_candidates.title: CSLib Tableau: private lemmas cause cross-file re-derivation at scale
memory_candidates.content: In Cslib/Logics/Modal/Tableau/, 77 comment-attested 'Local re-derivation of X (unavailable across files)' sites exist because FmpMeasure.lean marks 50 declarations private. modalSubfmls_trans is re-derived in three files (S5Simplification.lean:97, FiveSimplification.lean:736, BDriver.lean:211); modalKnownWorlds_fold_spec in four; hasEdge_addEdge_cases in four. Prefer private only for genuinely file-local helpers; a lemma another module will need must be public. Deduplicating this is mechanical and behaviour-preserving by construction, and it shrinks oversized files before anyone splits them.

memory_candidates.title: Tableau loop-check blocking: record an identification, not an edge
memory_candidates.content: When a modal tableau loop-check blocks a minting step, adding an accessibility edge src -> wBlock creates a soundness obligation m.r (f src) (f wBlock) that an existentially-quantified witness model cannot supply. Both source calculi avoid this: Massacci2000 Definition 10.2's SST-interpretation is explicitly not required injective, so the blocked world is identified with its shorter modal copy, and Pruning Lemma 8.2 deletes the descendant-closed subtree rather than linking to it; ChagrovZakharyaschev1997 Theorem 5.51 constructs the relation as a subset of the ambient one (S_{n+1} subset R_Grz) so the box-propagation condition (HSm1) is immediate. Diagnostic: if the completeness side constructs its model (extractModelWith Relation.ReflTransGen) while the soundness side quantifies existentially over an arbitrary model, the two disagree about what a model is, and a loop-back edge is harmless to one and fatal to the other.

memory_candidates.title: Lemmon box-plus keys are free in a subformula-indexed world bound
memory_candidates.content: Enriching filtration or birth keys from the unwrapped psi to the Lemmon box-plus pair {psi, box psi} costs nothing in a world bound of the form 2^(2*|Sub phi|), because modalSubfmls (.box a) = .box a :: modalSubfmls a makes box psi already a member of Sub phi whenever T(box psi)@w sits on a universe-closed branch. Why box-plus rather than psi alone: y satisfying psi AND box psi makes the filtration constraint composable across a further step, whereas psi alone tells you nothing about the next world (ChagrovZakharyaschev1997, print p. 142). Corollary 5.32 names S4 explicitly as admitting filtration via the Lemmon construction. The source never iterates box-plus beyond depth 1; where more discriminating power is needed it enlarges the filter Sigma instead (Theorems 5.34/5.35 use {box theta -> theta, dia box theta}), which DOES change the codomain and is therefore expensive. Enrich with box-plus, not with the filter. Caveat: the Lemmon filtration is defined for transitive models only, so this is not a Foundations-level abstraction.
